Every sensor and vision part, with what it detects, its range, its settings and its signals in each configuration, from the page’s own reference.

Fill Level Sensor (liquid in the bottle)

  • Settings: Fill line (px above the belt; a small bottle is 40 tall, a large 56; the liquid tops out at about 80 % of that); Sensor; Analog output (adds a Percent analog input: fill of the bottle under the sensor, 0-100 % of its label)
TagController I/OTypeDescription
Device_DetectInputBOOLLiquid at or above the fill line in the bottle under the sensor

Diffuse Sensor (photoelectric)

Diffuse photoelectric sensor: its own light reflects off the part, so no reflector is needed. The shaded band on the lane shows the sensing range.

  • LED: Red: detecting.
  • Detectable: Solids: any part.
  • Sensing range: 0 – 100 px, default 20 px (≈ 0.3 m). Factory I/O: 0 – 1.6 m.
  • Settings: Sensing range (px; 60 px = 1 m); Sensitivity (%): the gain. 100 sees every part at full range; lower it and the range shrinks and dull targets (glass bottles, broken glass, dark cartons) drop out before bright ones (metal, cans, white and yellow cartons); Beam; Sees
TagController I/OTypeDescription
Device_DetectInputBOOLDetecting: a solid part is within range

Retroreflective Sensor and Reflector

The sensor and its reflector face each other across the conveyor. Detect is 1 while the beam is interrupted. Use the beam height to ignore low parts: a lid (8 px) passes under a 12 px beam, a carton does not.

  • LED: Green: aligned with the reflector. Yellow: beam not interrupted (goes out while a part blocks it).
  • Detectable: Solids taller than the beam height.
  • Sensing range: Across the lane (≈ 1 m here; the real device reaches 6 m).
  • Settings: Beam height (px above the belt)
TagController I/OTypeDescription
Device_DetectInputBOOLLight beam interrupted

Light Array (8 beams)

Eight parallel beams form a light curtain. Beam 1 is lowest. Digital gives one BOOL per beam, Numerical packs the beams into one INT (bit 0 = beam 1), Analog gives 10 V × interrupted beams ÷ 8 as hundredths of a volt. With the default 6 px spacing a small carton (22 px) breaks beams 1-4, a medium one 5, a large one 7, a crate all 8, a lid only beam 1.

  • LED: Green: emitter and receiver synchronised. One red LED per interrupted beam.
  • Detectable: Solids; measures how tall a part is.
  • Sensing range: Across the lane; 8 beams spaced by the beam-spacing setting.
  • Settings: Output; Beam spacing (px of part height)

Inductive Sensor (metal)

Proximity sensor for metal. Digital gives Detect. Analog gives Volts: 0 V with the part at the sensor, rising to 10 V (1000) at the edge of the range, and 1000 when nothing metal is in range.

  • LED: Red: detecting.
  • Detectable: Conductive parts only: metal blocks, metal stock, metal bases and lids, cans.
  • Sensing range: 0 – 60 px, default 10 px (≈ 0.17 m). Factory I/O: 0 – 0.1 m.
  • Settings: Output; Sensing range (px; 60 px = 1 m)

Configuration: digital

TagController I/OTypeDescription
Device_DetectInputBOOLDetecting: a conductive (metal) part is within range

Configuration: analog

TagController I/OTypeDescription
Device_VoltsInputINT0–10 V as hundredths of a volt: distance from the sensor to the nearest metal part, 1000 when none in range

Capacitive Sensor (any material)

Short-range proximity sensor for anything. Digital gives Detect. Analog gives Volts exactly like the inductive sensor, without the material filter.

  • LED: Green: detecting.
  • Detectable: Any material: solids (and liquids on the real device).
  • Sensing range: 0 – 60 px, default 12 px (≈ 0.2 m), same as the real sensor.
  • Settings: Output; Sensing range (px; 60 px = 1 m)

Configuration: digital

TagController I/OTypeDescription
Device_DetectInputBOOLDetecting: any solid part is within range

Configuration: analog

TagController I/OTypeDescription
Device_VoltsInputINT0–10 V as hundredths of a volt: distance from the sensor to the nearest part, 1000 when none in range

Color Sensor (R/B/G/Y banks)

Four colour banks, one BOOL each.

  • LED: The head shows the colour it sees.
  • Detectable: Coloured plastic parts: red, blue, green, yellow. Metal gives no bank.
  • Sensing range: Directly beneath the head.
TagController I/OTypeDescription
Device_RedInputBOOLBank 1: red
Device_BlueInputBOOLBank 2: blue
Device_GreenInputBOOLBank 3: green
Device_YellowInputBOOLBank 4: yellow

Vision Sensor

Recognises the part under it. Digital: one BOOL per ticked part. Bits: the part code as five binary inputs Bit0-Bit4 (Factory I/O's "All Digital"). Numerical: one INT with the part code (the number next to each part in the list; 0 = none or not ticked). ID: the serial number of the part in view plus its code, usable like a barcode. Size: the older Small/Medium/Large/Metal outputs. Tick Triggered for a Trigger output with Busy and Complete, like a real smart camera: the result then holds until the next trigger. Set Inspection job to Bottle inspection and it checks a bottle's cap, label and fill instead: Pass is a bottle with all three, and on a camera module the result code is bit 0 no cap, bit 1 no label, bit 2 short fill, bit 3 no part in view, with the fill in % of the label in byte 9 of Inspection_Results. On a camera module, Buffer_Results_Enable queues results up to the buffer depth until the PLC acknowledges each one (Results_Buffer_Overrun when one is lost). A Process HMI set to show the sensor draws its camera screen. Card mode (bottle job): the bottle cards SN-4801 to SN-4804 decide each bottle. The hopper sends plain good bottles; when a result comes back, the bottle under the camera takes the card's verdict (no cap, no label, short fill; no card in view makes it a reject) and moves on. Each bottle waits at the camera until its result is presented, so there is time to swap the card. With the simulated camera, pick the card in Card under the lens or on the camera screen's CARDS page; with the camera module live on a real In-Sight, the real card decides: its result code, the fill in byte 9 and the card ID in byte 10 of Inspection_Results.

  • LED: Green: a part in view. Amber: result valid for a selected part. The ring light flashes on a trigger.
  • Detectable: Every part in the catalogue; tick the ones to detect.
  • Sensing range: Directly beneath the camera.
  • Settings: Output; Camera module (its name in I/O Configuration; blank = wired signals only); Housing; Parts to Detect; Triggered (adds Trigger input, Busy and Complete); Inspection time (ms); Inspection job; Card job: the inspection line it looks down on (blank = the first); Card job: the TCP Client Socket that sends it the recipe string (blank = the first); Bottle job: the fill passes at (% of the label); Results buffer depth (camera module, with Buffer_Results_Enable on); Card mode (bottle job): the card under the camera decides what is wrong with each bottle, and each bottle waits at the camera for its result; Camera jobs, in job ID order: PRODUCT:min fill %, … (Level 12; blank = the one job above); Card under the lens (simulated camera; a live camera reads the real card); Live image: after each inspection of a live camera, fetch the image it acquired (image.bmp, over FTP through the bridge) and show it on the camera screen; Live image: FTP user on the camera (a user with FTP Read); Live image: FTP password (blank for the In-Sight default admin); Live image: at most one image every (s) — each image is work for the camera; Live image: width to fetch (px; the bridge scales the image down to this); Live camera: where the inspection ID and result code are read

RFID Reader

Single-trigger command interface: set Command, pulse Execute; when CommandID increments the command has finished and Status says how it went (0 = success). Command 0 only checks for a tag, 1 reads the serial into ReadData, 2 reads the word at MemoryIndex, 3 writes WriteData there, 4 clears the memory. Two tags in range give status 2. Write a route code into a part at one station and sort on it at the next.

  • LED: Green: idle. Orange: executing a command. Red: the last command failed.
  • Detectable: RFID tags. Every part carries one except raw stock, housing bases and housing lids. Each tag has a unique serial number and 16 words of memory.
  • Sensing range: 0 – 60 px, default 16 px.
  • Settings: Reading range (px); Command time (ms)
TagController I/OTypeDescription
Device_CommandOutputINTCommand to execute: 0 = is a tag available?, 1 = read serial number, 2 = read data, 3 = write data, 4 = clear all data
Device_ExecuteOutputBOOLRising edge executes the command
Device_MemoryIndexOutputINTTag memory index for read/write (0-15)
Device_WriteDataOutputINTData written by command 3
Device_CommandIDInputINTNumber of commands executed so far; changes when the current one has finished
Device_StatusInputINT0 = success, 1 = no tag, 2 = too many tags, 3 = invalid index, 4 = invalid command
Device_ReadDataInputINTResult of command 1 (serial) or 2 (data)
Device_TagPresentInputBOOLExactly one tag is within range

Code Reader (DataMan 260 series, EtherNet/IP)

A fixed-mount code reader of the Cognex DataMan 260 series (the DM262 and kin) on EtherNet/IP. It has no wired signals: it works on its module's tags. Type the module's name into Reader module, or use Add DataMan Module in its properties. The handshake is the reader's own: set Trigger_Enable; a 0 → 1 on Trigger with Trigger_Ready on takes an image (hold Trigger until Trigger_Ack); after the decode time Results_Available comes on with Result_ID (the trigger it answers), Result_Code (bit 0 = read, bit 1 = matches the match string), Result_Length and the string in Result_Data; set Results_Ack and drop it once Results_Available clears. Buffer_Results_Enable queues results until each is acknowledged; a result that finds the queue full is lost and Results_Buffer_Overrun says so. A trigger while it is busy is missed (Missed_Acq, and bit 3 on the next result). SoftEvent 1 trains the match string from the next read, 4 clears it, 7 sets it from User_Data. Add Example Routine writes a routine with the whole handshake. Click the reader in Run mode for its screen. Implicit mode: the module talks to your reader through the bridge and the part shows what the real reader decoded.

  • LED: On top: green ready (Trigger_Ready), green good read, red fault or no read. The window's illumination LEDs flash on each trigger; the field across the lane turns green on a read, orange on a no read.
  • Detectable: The code on a part: the date coder's mark on a bottle, or a code label from the emitter (Code labels).
  • Sensing range: Across the lane, the field of view along the belt (default 12 px, 0.2 m): a part is read when its centre is in it.
  • Settings: Reader module (its name in I/O Configuration); Field of view along the belt (px; 60 px = 1 m): a code whose part is centred in it can be read; Reading height above the belt (px); Decode time (ms, the simulated reader); Result queue with Buffer_Results_Enable (results the simulated reader holds); Illumination; Symbologies the reader decodes (the rest are no reads, like Disable Untrained Symbologies); Live: show the reader's last image (through the bridge); Live: reader user (Telnet); Live: reader password; Live: reader Telnet port
TagController I/OTypeDescription

Card Sort Cell (bench fixture: magazine, nest, PASS and FAIL trays; 5603 and DataMan over the nest)

  • Settings: Camera that looks into the nest (a Vision Sensor's name); Code reader that looks into the nest (a Code Reader's name); TCP Client Socket that talks to the camera (the simulated camera takes LOT n from it and answers after each inspection); The simulated camera's answer over TCP ({code} result code, {read} the lot code read or NOREAD, {card} card ID, {result} PASS or FAIL); Magazine order; Card motion
TagController I/OTypeDescription
Device_Card_In_NestInputBOOLA card is in the nest

Device_Sorted_PassInputBOOLPulse: a card went into the PASS tray
Device_Sorted_FailInputBOOLPulse: a card went into the FAIL tray
